reviewContext.issueReference: workflowInput:RESUME-session-269 'RESUME session 269: serial perf gate for large-eval, accept EDITCOST/RUNSTART, silent CANVAS-EVIDENCE measurement, final review and closeout' (workflowExecutionId opus-luna-design-and-implement-review-loop-session-271, chain 265-266-267-269-271; operator decision P; design accepted by step3-design-review comm-004102; plans accepted by step5-impl-plan-review comm-004104; no GitHub issue number)
reviewContext.userProblem: The production vactr editor still renders through CodeMirror EditorView (15 production files import @codemirror/view), visuals follow message receipt or raw AudioContext.currentTime instead of audible time, native output latency is always 'unavailable', the Tauri shell has no IPC or iOS project, and there is no real-browser evidence. The user wants a GPU canvas code editor for browsers and iPad with audio-clock synchronized visuals, bounded resources and measured evidence.
requiredOutcomes: Design amendment 15.3.8 covering song mode, completion popup, format/syntax migration, frame scheduler and backgrounding, ABI batch bounds and incremental deltas, and the measurement protocol with numeric thresholds (accepted; committed in this checkpoint).
WebGL2 canvas renders code text, cursor, selection, syntax, diagnostics and playing highlights; DOM is only the input, IME, clipboard and accessibility bridge (CANVAS-RENDER, CANVAS-MOUNT).
One headless EditorState authority with revisions and undo/redo; zero @codemirror/view or EditorView in production editor/src, enforced by editor/test/canvas/no-editor-view.test.ts (CANVAS-MOUNT).
Formatting, completion, evaluation, parameter editing/binding, diagnostics and song mode work on the canvas surface, with ported tests that keep their assertions (CANVAS-MOUNT).

AudibleClock with output-timestamp or probe correlation, epochs, staleness hide and late-frame recovery without drift or replayed flashes drives highlights, the transport bar, scopes, Hydra and video (CANVAS-CLOCK, CANVAS-VISUAL).
Native CPAL output-clock correlation publishing real latency provenance and a Session Protocol clock-probe; audio callback adds only a non-blocking record call (CANVAS-NATIVE).
Tauri desktop Session Protocol IPC tier and a Tauri iOS project built and launched on an iPad simulator with audio-session glue, or an exact blocker recorded (CANVAS-SHELL).
Animation-only frames do zero shaping, atlas uploads and buffer uploads; per-frame atlas budget, caps and disposal are tested (CANVAS-RENDER).

Playwright-library harness in Chromium and WebKit with behavioral checks and measurements on a 20,000-line ~1 MiB document, harness-written evidence in design-docs/specs/design-canvas-editor-evidence.md, honest limitations and pending physical-iPad procedures, final gates and closeout archival (CANVAS-EVIDENCE).

Session 269 (design 15.3.8.10): a one-character edit and a word delete on the 20,000-line document make no Text.toString call and no slice over 64 KiB; DocumentSync byte conversion is line-based and byte-identical to Utf8Index; syntax providers use Text identity, chunked tree-sitter input and line-local fallback tokenizing (CANVAS-EVIDENCE-EDITCOST).

Session 269: the large-document eval fix is gated by a 2x focused-median budget, three consecutive green full vitest runs, bounded pre-fix mutation evidence, strict clippy and outside-sandbox full nextest (CANVAS-EVIDENCE-RUNSTART).

Session 271 (design 15.3.8.11): no absolute wall-clock assertion in the default vitest suite; the 2x focused-median budget runs only in npm run test:perf (VACTR_PERF=1, --maxWorkers=1, run alone); EDITCOST and RUNSTART are accepted on three consecutive default full vitest runs plus test:perf (CANVAS-EVIDENCE-RUNSTART, CANVAS-EVIDENCE-EDITCOST).
nonGoals: No resume or repair of the canvas-editor-224 dispatch, snapshot, fingerprint or recovery contracts.
No @codemirror/autocomplete or other view-bound extensions; no new runtime dependency and no lockfile change.
No Apple provisioning profiles, uploads or signing-identity changes; simulator and unsigned builds only.
No physical-iPad, real-IME-hardware, VoiceOver-on-device or physical audio-latency claims.

Session 267 (design 15.3.8.9): product defects found by the harness are fixed in their owner files by the wave-3 plans CANVAS-EVIDENCE-VIEWPORT, -EDITCOST and -RUNSTART, never recorded as acceptable; CANVAS-EVIDENCE itself (wave 4) changes no product code.
No change to the production master output stage, no system audio driver install, never read or change macOS system volume (operator decision S).
No crate-wide cargo fmt and no edit of the untracked .agents/settings.local.json.
constraints: Work only on wf/canvas; non-force push to origin wf/canvas is authorized; no push to main, no PRs.

The suite stays green before each acceptance: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0, full nextest (timeout >= 1500 s; a timeout kill is neither pass nor fail), npm run check exit 0, full vitest pass with no assertion deleted.
Touched Rust or TypeScript source files must stay under 1000 lines.
Audio processing never waits on, allocates for, or is driven by rendering; visuals read published telemetry only.
Codex sandbox cannot bind localhost and keeps .git read-only: Playwright, HTTP servers, simulator launches and full nextest run in outside-sandbox verification steps.
Implementers record fresh-read and post-edit sha256 values under tmp/canvas-cutover/<plan>/; within a wave writePaths are disjoint; sharedPaths are edited only for the recorded reason.

Session 271 (operator decision P): absolute wall-clock budgets never run inside the default parallel vitest suite; they run only in the dedicated serial perf gate cd editor && npm run test:perf (--maxWorkers=1), alone on the host; perf files are excluded from the default run by vitest config, never by skipping, deleting or env-gating an assertion.
designDecisionsAndRationale: Headless @codemirror/state EditorState is the single document authority because history and transactions are already tested; EditorView is removed entirely (15.3.8.2).
The separate CONSUMERS plan is merged into MOUNT so the frozen surface contract and every consumer migration land in one green change (15.3.8.1, 15.3.8.9).

Text redraw is driven by document/viewport revisions and is separate from the animation loop; hidden pages stop rAF while audio continues, and resume re-derives positions from the audible clock (15.3.8.3).

The clock-probe wire keeps the existing tested field names (page_send, engine_receive, engine_send; kind clock-probe) instead of the design's draft names; EVIDENCE appends the erratum at closeout (clock.md:36-44).
Both native transports (WebSocket and Tauri IPC) share one Session Protocol clock-probe instead of a Tauri-specific probe (15.3.8.5).
A shorter headless gating measurement profile replaces 15.3.7 product durations for headless runs; physical-device profile stays pending (15.3.8.8).
The evidence harness writes raw data and the results section itself so no hand-typed numbers are committed (evidence.md:21-24).

Session 271 (15.3.8.11): large-eval splits into a contention-insensitive default file (one eval-result, zero error diagnostics, 20k/5k ratio <= 6) and editor/test/e2e/large-eval.perf.test.ts (absolute budget ceil(2*m/100)*100 ms) sharing large-eval-shared.ts, because session 269 showed the 4,800 ms budget failing only under default-worker contention (exits 0, 1, 1) while --maxWorkers=1 runs passed 696/696 three times.
intentionalTradeoffs: WebKit clipboard, IME and touch checks use synthetic events and are labeled limitations.
Hydra outputs are measured at the shipping 640x360 RENDER_SIZE instead of the 15.3.7 1024x1024 workload; recorded as a deviation (L-WORKLOAD-SIZE accepted limitation).
The gen/apple file list is derived from tauri-cli templates rather than an executed ios init; up to 5 recorded additions are allowed and an app-name mismatch is a recorded blocker.
counters().probe in window.__vactrPerf may be null if AudibleClock does not expose its ProbeCorrelation (L-PROBE-STATS-REACH, low); no gated metric depends on it.
Native and iPad video composition are listed as unavailable in the evidence document.
supportedEdgeCases: Japanese IME composition, grapheme-aware cursor and delete, emoji and lines over 400 columns.
WebGL context loss and restore with an unchanged document; GPU-unavailable status.
devicePixelRatio changes, resize and visualViewport keyboard insets.
Page backgrounding with zero rAF while hidden and no replayed flashes on return.
Suspended AudioContext treated as an invalid correlation; 'unavailable' probe replies stay valid with explicit provenance.
Stale or cross-epoch transport samples rejected; scopes hidden after 2 s without fresh data.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Physical-iPad latency, A/V sync, frame time and memory measurements (recorded as pending procedures).
Real IME hardware and VoiceOver on device.
Signed device builds, provisioning and distribution.
Native and iPad video background composition.

executionModel.implementer: GPT-6 Luna (Codex) per plan, native fanout on wf/canvas
rules: The accepted design and all plans are committed and pushed before wave 1 starts.
Within a wave, source writePaths are disjoint. sharedPaths are conditional seams, edited only for the stated reason and recorded in the owning plan's progress log.

artifactRoots (session 266, operator decision A): each plan lists the gitignored build and test outputs it may write. Every artifactRoots entry is also listed in that plan's writePaths and never in sharedPaths. The common roots target, tree-sitter-vact/tree-sitter-vact.wasm, editor/node_modules/.vite, editor/dist, editor/src-tauri/target and editor/src-tauri/gen/schemas are intentionally declared by several plans of one wave: they are gitignored tool outputs (Cargo and Vite take their own locks; the grammar build is idempotent), recorded as digest manifests, and never committed. Tracked files, including the generated gen/apple project files SHELL commits, stay ordinary writePaths. If a command writes a gitignored in-repo path outside the declared roots, stop, record the path in the plan's progress log, and amend the manifest serially before acceptance.

Setup is not gating: each plan's setup list prepares gitignored prerequisites in a clean snapshot (grammar wasm only when absent, then the host-wasm library build) and is not reported as verification.

Rule D (session 266, every implementer and verifier): the gating verification list contains only final-source commands that are expected to pass. Mutation and negative-control runs go to a separate mutationEvidence list with command, expected nonzero exit, actual exit and complete log path. A re-run after a fixed failure replaces the failed run in the gating list; the failed run, superseded compile failures and selector typos appear only in history notes.

Each implementer records fresh-read sha256 values before each edit and post-edit hashes in its tmp/canvas-cutover/<plan>/intent.json and receipt.json. Drift in a not-yet-edited file stops edits to that file; repair is serial after the join.
The suite must be green before each acceptance: npm run check exit 0, full vitest pass, clippy -D warnings exit 0, full nextest pass (timeout >= 1500 s; a timeout kill is neither pass nor fail).
Implementers run focused checks in the sandbox. Playwright, HTTP servers, simulator launches and full nextest runs happen in the verification and review steps outside the sandbox.
No crate-wide cargo fmt; rustfmt only on touched files. Never edit .agents/settings.local.json. No new dependencies; no lockfile changes.
impl-plans/README.md and archival moves are edited only by CANVAS-EVIDENCE closeout, serially.

Session 267 wave 3: the four plans run concurrently on wf/canvas with disjoint source writePaths. A full-vitest failure located only in another wave-3 plan's files is reported with its log path and not fixed by the observing implementer; the post-join verification run is authoritative.

Session 267 silence rule: every automated browser run installs the CANVAS-EVIDENCE-SILENT virtual sink and launches Chromium with --mute-audio; a run whose post-sink peak is not exactly 0 or that has a direct destination connection fails, regardless of other results.

Session 269: SILENT and VIEWPORT are acceptedDependencies (commit 6f6b807) and are not redispatched. Wave 3 is EDITCOST and RUNSTART in parallel with disjoint writePaths; a full-vitest failure located only in the other plan's files is reported, not fixed; the post-join verification (including RUNSTART's three consecutive full vitest runs and outside-sandbox full nextest) is authoritative.

Session 269 (design 15.3.8.10): wall-clock vitest budgets equal 2x the median of three focused runs on the final source, rounded up to 100 ms; widening a harness timeout to hide a slow product path is forbidden; mutation evidence is reported separately and never gates.

Session 269: CANVAS-EVIDENCE seam sharedPaths are edited only under the seam protocol in impl-plans/active/canvas-cutover-evidence.md (Session 269 Amendment); a product defect in any other file goes to its owning accepted plan by selective redispatch.

Session 271 (design 15.3.8.11, supersedes the session-269 wall-clock rule): absolute wall-clock budgets live only in editor/test/**/*.perf.test.ts and run only through cd editor && npm run test:perf (VACTR_PERF=1 vitest run --maxWorkers=1), alone on the host with no concurrent vitest, nextest, cargo or browser run; a failed perf run is a failure, never retried until it passes. The default ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run excludes perf files by config and contains no absolute ms budget; no assertion is skipped, deleted or env-gated inside a file.

Session 271 waves: RUNSTART (wave 3) runs alone; EDITCOST (wave 4, gates-only) depends on RUNSTART; CANVAS-EVIDENCE (wave 5) depends on both. Acceptance of EDITCOST and RUNSTART requires three consecutive default full vitest runs (exit 0 each) plus npm run test:perf (exit 0, alone), npm run check, strict clippy, rustfmt --check on the six RUNSTART Rust files and outside-sandbox full nextest (timeout >= 1500 s).
